name: Anonymous (Plains nations)
language: Arapaho, Cheyenne, Comanche, Paiute, Kiowa, Caddo, Lakota
bio: The Ghost Dance songs were sung in the religious movement that spread from the Paiute prophet Wovoka across the Plains and the West in 1889–1891, promising the return of the dead and the renewal of the old world. Each nation made its own songs in its own language, and they were sung in the circle dance.

They were written down between 1890 and 1893 by the ethnologist James Mooney (1861–1921), who printed the native texts with his English renderings in The Ghost-Dance Religion and the Sioux Outbreak of 1890 (1896).
